quiz.question: What happens when you try to access a variable outside the function where it was created?

answers.answer: You get an error because the variable is not defined outside that function
It works fine because all variables are global

quiz.explanation: Variables created inside a function only exist within that function's scope. Trying to access them outside causes a 'not defined' error.

quiz.question: Why is scope considered a good thing in programming?

answers.answer: It keeps variables contained so different parts of your program don't accidentally interfere with each other
It allows you to skip writing function definitions

quiz.explanation: Scope prevents accidental conflicts between variables in different parts of your program by keeping them contained to where they were created.
